text.p: GreenStone Industries Inc. said on Tuesday it signed a letter of intent to be acquired by Lousiana-Pacific Corp.

GreenStone shareholders would receive $5.25 per share in cash, GreenStone said in a statement. Management and certain non-public shareholders would receive non-registered shares of Lousiana-Pacific of the equivalent value, the company said.
The transaction was expected to close by the end of calendar 1996, Greenstone said.

GreenStone Industries is a make of high quality cellulose insulation and specialty fibers from recycled paper -- primarily old newspaper. The company operates eight manufacturing facilities throughout the United States and had annual sales in 1995 of $41 million, Lousiana-Pacific said in a separate statement confirming the deal.
"GreenStone is an excellent fit with our strategic plan as we focus on value-added products that can grow rapidly," said Mark A. Suwyn, Lousiana-Pacific's Chairman and CEO.

Completion of the acquisition was subject to due diligence by Lousiana-Pacific, execution of a definitive purchase agreement, regulatory filings, approval by Greenstone shareholders and other actions.
